text: A new C++ ground node fits the floor plane from the 10 Hz ToF cloud with an IMU prior and gives plane-relative obstacle, step and drop-off marks; only real data is published.

The plane-relative marks feed Nav2 alongside the current fixed bands (switch-over only after validation, criteria documented); the collision monitor keeps the 10 Hz ToF; the global costmap stays static + lidar; no depth-bias correction in this epic.
The ground estimate (floor height, slope with the tilt_guard cross-check, steps and drop-offs as surface regions) is available to consumers: mcp_server map summary and floor_guard Terrain.
RGB-D colour labels floor vs obstacle, and the ground estimate is visible in the web UI map.
Ansible node type with the ros2_nodes schema and a cgroup tier, metrics with a Grafana panel, and the CPU budget measured on the Pi 5.
READMEs, tests/README.md, MEMORY entry, runbook and a final robot verification executed after merge.
